brand.title: ESourceAIG (Production)
brand.subtitle: Knowledge Check — Build Your Professional Portfolio with ChatGPT Sites

questions.question: What is the primary goal you will have completed by the end of this course?
choices: A complete, visitor-ready portfolio site with the skills to keep improving it
A perfect résumé that never needs to be updated
A social media profile across all major platforms
A printed portfolio book distributed to hiring managers
questions.feedback_correct: Exactly right—the course equips you with a polished portfolio and the ongoing skills to refine it continuously.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The course focuses on building a complete portfolio site and developing your ability to improve it over time, not on creating static résumés or printed materials.

questions.question: According to the course, what should you gather before you start building your portfolio site?
choices: Only a professional headshot and your LinkedIn URL
Career documents, work evidence, and personal assets like résumés, project samples, and a professional headshot
A perfectly polished résumé and at least five years of work history
Testimonials from at least ten clients before you begin
questions.feedback_correct: You've got it—gathering existing career documents, work samples, and personal assets gives you everything you need to start.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The course emphasizes that you likely already have most of what you need. You should collect career documents, work evidence, and personal assets before building, without waiting for perfection.

questions.question: What is the key difference between a portfolio and a résumé, according to this course?
choices: A portfolio uses color while a résumé is black and white
A portfolio is longer and more detailed than a résumé
The difference is not format—it is proof that shows results and context, not just listed experience
A portfolio is only for creative professionals, while a résumé is for everyone
questions.feedback_correct: Perfect—a portfolio tells the full story with evidence, while a résumé simply lists what you've done, leaving questions unanswered.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The course emphasizes that the real difference is proof. A portfolio shows the challenge you faced, actions you took, results you achieved, and what you learned—not just a longer list of experiences.

questions.question: What is the Portfolio Promise, and what question must your site answer?
choices: A promise to update your site weekly and respond to all visitors within 24 hours
The answer to 'Why should this person be trusted with important work?'—and you have 30 seconds to make it clear
A guarantee that your site will rank first on Google search results
A promise to include at least ten case studies and client testimonials
questions.feedback_correct: Exactly—the Portfolio Promise is about establishing trust immediately by answering why someone should trust you with important work within the first 30 seconds.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The Portfolio Promise is fundamentally about trust and making your value proposition crystal clear right at the top. You have limited time—about 30 seconds—to answer this core question.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT mentioned as a benchmark for a strong first portfolio site?
choices: Easy to Scan and Specific
Honest and Audience-Aware
Evidence-Based and Clear Next Steps
Maximum length of at least 50 pages with extensive multimedia
questions.feedback_correct: Right—length and complexity are not benchmarks. The course emphasizes that a strong portfolio should be clear, not complex.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The six actual benchmarks are: Easy to Scan, Specific, Honest, Audience-Aware, Evidence-Based, and Clear Next Steps. The course teaches that complexity isn't necessary—clarity is what matters most.

questions.question: What does the course recommend you do immediately after your site first appears, before making any edits?
choices: Start editing sections that look generic or unclear
Publish it immediately to get visitor feedback
Pause and ask five critical questions to evaluate objectively what feels strong, generic, missing, too long, and what a visitor would understand in 30 seconds
Share it with everyone on social media to build initial traffic
questions.feedback_correct: Perfect—the course teaches you to resist the urge to immediately edit and instead step back to evaluate objectively first.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The course emphasizes that diagnosis comes before editing. Take time to ask critical questions about what's working and what isn't, rather than jumping into changes right away.

questions.question: According to the 3-Pass Edit activity, what is the focus of Pass 3?
choices: Clarify the message and check if your introduction is instantly clear
Strengthen your evidence by adding quantified accomplishments and specific impact stories
Improve the layout and ensure the site is scannable with clear headings
Check for spelling and grammar errors
questions.feedback_correct: Great—Pass 3 focuses on strengthening your evidence with concrete results and impact, which builds credibility.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The three passes are: Pass 1 (Clarify the message), Pass 2 (Improve the layout), and Pass 3 (Strengthen your evidence). Each pass has a specific, focused goal.

questions.question: How does the course recommend you handle confidential or sensitive work when presenting it in your portfolio?
choices: Avoid mentioning any work that involves confidentiality agreements
Share all details to show your full capabilities and expertise
Present your work professionally without revealing information you should not share, and anonymize details when needed
Only include work from clients who explicitly gave you permission to show everything
questions.feedback_correct: Exactly—you can showcase your accomplishments and expertise while respecting NDAs and confidentiality agreements by being strategic about what you disclose.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The course teaches that you should balance transparency with discretion. You can share your work accomplishments while respecting confidentiality—use anonymization when needed and never disclose proprietary information without permission.

questions.question: What is a Portfolio AI Teammate, and how does it differ from just using ChatGPT during the course?
choices: It's a different AI tool that only works with portfolio websites and costs extra to use
A personal assistant that works for you continuously—capturing accomplishments as they happen, helping create case studies, and keeping your portfolio current long after the course ends
A one-time feature that ChatGPT Sites provides during the initial portfolio build
A team of actual humans who help you manage your portfolio website
questions.feedback_correct: Spot on—your AI Teammate is an ongoing tool that continues supporting your career growth beyond the course, capturing wins as they happen and helping you stay current.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The Portfolio AI Teammate is not a one-time tool—it's designed to be a continuous part of your professional growth system, helping you capture new accomplishments, create case studies while projects are fresh, and customize versions for different audiences.

questions.question: What does the course describe as the end result of completing its full program?
choices: A static website that showcases your past experience
A professional storytelling system combining your experience, evidence, ChatGPT Sites, and an AI teammate that you continue using long after the course ends
A résumé that is optimized for applicant tracking systems
A social media presence that drives traffic to your portfolio
questions.feedback_correct: Excellent—the course aims to create a dynamic, ongoing system, not just a one-time website. Your AI teammate continues to support your career growth well beyond the course.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The course is designed to build a professional storytelling system that evolves with you. It's not just a static website or résumé—it's a tool and approach you'll use continuously for ongoing career development.
